correctness.rationale: For each signal state, the gain is supported only by the two disjoint cases in which a critical background vote count makes one of the designated voters pivotal, with opposite outcomes under direct and delegated voting. Equal adjacent binomial coefficients give the exact finite-size identity; dividing by a positive exponential leaves an affine monotone exponential, proving at most one crossing. Exact-rational complete-vector enumeration and separate probability convolution agree in 220 parameter configurations; a closed-form five-voter check yields 2/625 and three-voter check yields -1/375. No numerical approximation is used as an all-size proof.

originality.rationale: The model and conditional independence are shared with Gilbert et al. (arXiv:2608.16738v1, full HTML sections 2-5 and appendices available), but its all-to-one/paired finite-size numerical constructions and asymptotic local-mechanism results neither state nor establish the exact single-edge two-exponential size law. Kahng et al. (JAIR 2021) work with scalar independent competences; Abramowitz--Mattei (2024) use a fixed-representative model and voter-majority agreement. Targeted public literature and mathematical-record searches plus accessible prior-claim comparisons identified no stronger equivalent conclusion; residual priority risk remains for a potentially unindexed pivotal-probability identity.

value.rationale: The result isolates the population-size dependence of majority correctness for an intrinsically natural minimal delegation decision in the recently introduced correlated epistemic-voting model, despite identical statewise competence ranking. The exact one-crossing classification and rational reversal between the two smallest nontrivial odd electorates clarify why better information and better collective accuracy differ, and give an explicit finite-size decision rule. Its value comes from this coherent size-transition structure, not merely exact arithmetic.
